## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: circular versus arrow signals, steady versus flashing, broken signals, ramp meters and hybrid beacons
Confusable pairs among the traffic signal displays, each tied to one handbook page; hint metadata sits only in trailing lines.

FACT_ID: sec14-R01 | anchor: A01
A circular green lets you turn only after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, while a green arrow gives you a protected turn. [A01]
Why it matters: group green signals; difficulty high; confusable permitted versus protected.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec14-R02 | anchor: A01
A circular yellow means stop if you safely can, while a yellow arrow means the protected arrow phase is about to end. [A01]
Why it matters: group yellow signals; difficulty medium; confusable circle versus arrow.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec14-R03 | anchor: A01
A steady circular red still allows a right turn after a full stop unless signed otherwise, while a red arrow stops all turning traffic in that direction. [A01]
Why it matters: group red signals; difficulty high; confusable circle versus arrow.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec14-R04 | anchor: A02
A flashing red works like a stop sign and a flashing yellow works like a warning sign. [A02]
Why it matters: group flashing signals; difficulty medium; confusable stop versus caution.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec14-R05 | anchor: A02
A flashing yellow arrow means turn after yielding, while a solid yellow arrow means prepare to stop. [A02]
Why it matters: group yellow arrows; difficulty high; confusable flashing versus solid.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec14-R06 | anchor: A02
A dark or broken traffic signal means an all-way stop, unless an officer is directing traffic or another device is working. [A02]
Why it matters: group malfunctions; difficulty medium; misconception target.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec14-R07 | anchor: A03
A ramp meter showing red means stop and wait, but a ramp meter showing nothing at all means you may merge without stopping. [A03]
Why it matters: group ramp meters; difficulty high; confusable red versus dark display.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec14-R08 | anchor: A03
At a hybrid beacon, steady red means stay stopped, while flashing red lets you go after a full stop once the crossing is clear. [A03]
Why it matters: group hybrid beacons; difficulty high; confusable steady versus flashing red.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec14-R09 | anchor: A03
A hybrid beacon begins with flashing yellow and then steady yellow before red, unlike a ramp meter that shows only red or green. [A03]
Why it matters: group beacon sequence; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0084]
